FR-001.title: The system MUST resolve every player connection to exactly one server-recognized logical session.

FR-002.title: A logical session MUST have an opaque stable identity for the lifetime of the current server process.

FR-003.title: A newly established logical session MUST receive a unique automatically generated fallback display name.

FR-004.title: The game master MUST be able to rename a logical session's fallback display name without changing its identity, character assignment, control status, or terminal state.

FR-005.title: Reopening, refreshing, reconnecting, navigating away and returning, or reopening the browser from the same recognized browser profile MUST reuse the same logical session while the server process remains active.

FR-006.title: Multiple tabs sharing one recognized browser identity MUST represent one logical session.

FR-007.title: A logical session MUST be connected while at least one of its player connections remains open.

FR-008.title: Closing one of several connections for a logical session MUST NOT disconnect the session or release its character.

FR-009.title: A different browser, browser profile, private-browsing context, cleared local identity, or otherwise unrecognized device context MUST establish a separate logical session.

FR-010.title: Establishing a new logical session MUST NOT release any claim held by an older disconnected session.

FR-011.title: Logical session identity and fallback-name changes MUST remain process-local and MUST expire when the server process restarts.

FR-012.title: Character assignments MUST belong to the current live broadcast rather than to an individual configured terminal.

FR-013.title: Switching active terminals, starting or finishing a puzzle, and disconnecting or reconnecting MUST NOT clear a valid current-broadcast character assignment.

FR-014.title: Ending a broadcast MUST clear every character claim and the active-controller assignment.

FR-015.title: Ending a broadcast MUST retain recognized logical sessions until server restart.

FR-016.title: Starting a new broadcast MUST require every logical session to obtain a new character assignment.

FR-017.title: A session identifier issued by a previous server process MUST restore none of its previous name, assignment, presence, or control state.

FR-018.title: Runtime session, fallback-name, presence, character-claim, and controller data MUST NOT be added to the persisted version-1 terminal/session schema.

FR-019.title: The game master MUST be able to define a roster of player characters before or during a live broadcast.

FR-020.title: Each roster entry MUST have a stable identity for the current server process, a player-facing name, and an available-or-claimed state.

FR-021.title: The game master MUST be able to add and rename roster entries without mutating logical sessions, controller status, or terminal state.

FR-022.title: Renaming a roster entry MUST update every affected game-master and player view without creating a new assignment.

FR-023.title: The system MUST refuse to delete a claimed roster entry until its claim is released or transferred.

FR-024.title: One logical session MUST have no more than one character assignment during a broadcast.

FR-025.title: One roster character MUST be claimed by no more than one logical session during a broadcast.

FR-026.title: Character availability and claim decisions MUST be authoritative at the server when each selection is processed.

FR-027.title: Concurrent claims for one character MUST result in exactly one successful claim.

FR-028.title: Concurrent different selections from one logical session MUST result in no more than one character assignment.

FR-029.title: A rejected claimant MUST remain unassigned and receive the current roster state.

FR-030.title: A disconnected session's character MUST remain claimed until release, transfer, broadcast end, or server restart.

FR-031.title: A player MUST NOT independently replace a completed character assignment.

FR-032.title: The game master MUST be able to assign an available character to an unassigned logical session.

FR-033.title: Releasing a character MUST make it available and return its connected former session to character selection without canonical terminal or puzzle mutation.

FR-034.title: Moving a character MUST remove it from the old session and assign it to the new session as one authoritative operation.

FR-035.title: Character release, correction, and transfer MUST NOT mutate terminal navigation, puzzle state, logs, attempts, randomness, or outcome.

FR-036.title: Player-facing roster state MUST distinguish available from claimed characters without exposing private connection information.

FR-037.title: No more than one character-assigned logical session MUST be designated active controller at any time.

FR-038.title: The first eligible character assignment processed while the broadcast has no established controller MUST atomically designate exactly one initial active controller.

FR-039.title: Character-assigned sessions completing selection while a controller exists MUST begin as observers.

FR-040.title: Raw connection order MUST NOT establish controller status before successful character assignment.

FR-041.title: Concurrent first-time assignments MUST establish exactly one active controller.

FR-042.title: Controller assignment MUST apply globally across the live broadcast and all configured terminals.

FR-043.title: The game master MUST be able to designate a connected, character-assigned observer as the active controller.

FR-044.title: Reassignment MUST make the selected session active and the previous active session an observer as one authoritative change.

FR-045.title: Controller reassignment MUST preserve character assignments and all canonical terminal and puzzle state.

FR-046.title: Releasing or moving the active session's character without explicit reassignment MUST clear controller assignment and MUST NOT promote an observer.

FR-047.title: When no eligible controller is designated, player terminal actions MUST remain read-only until game-master reassignment or a later eligible initial assignment establishes control.

FR-048.title: Disconnecting the active session MUST retain its active designation and character claim.

FR-049.title: Disconnecting the active session MUST NOT automatically promote or elect another session.

FR-050.title: Reconnecting the unchanged active session before reassignment MUST restore its ability to control the terminal.

FR-051.title: Reconnecting a former controller after game-master reassignment MUST restore it as an observer with its existing character.

FR-052.title: Disconnecting or reconnecting any session MUST NOT mutate terminal or puzzle state.

FR-053.title: A player action MUST be eligible for canonical processing only when its connection resolves to a current logical session with a valid current-broadcast character assignment.

FR-054.title: A terminal-mutating player action MUST be eligible only when the owning logical session is the active controller at processing time and is currently connected.

FR-055.title: Controller authorization MUST be enforced authoritatively for every player action rather than relying on disabled player controls.

FR-056.title: Observer, unassigned, unknown, expired, invalid, and stale-controller actions MUST leave all canonical state unchanged.

FR-057.title: Rejected player actions MUST NOT consume attempts, activate patterns, advance randomness, navigate content, alter logs, trigger outcomes, or otherwise mutate puzzle or terminal state.

FR-058.title: An unassigned session MUST NOT submit or cause terminal actions before character selection completes.

FR-059.title: The system MUST accept existing player-side navigation, menu, password-candidate, filler-character, special-pattern, and other terminal actions for canonical processing only from the active controller.

FR-060.title: Observer hover and focus feedback MUST remain local without submitting a shared action or changing canonical state.

FR-061.title: Any control available to an observer MUST be limited to client-local behavior that does not affect shared state.

FR-062.title: The player surface MUST present observer controls as visibly read-only within the existing terminal aesthetic.

FR-063.title: The player surface MUST expose no operation that invokes `ForceHackSuccess`.

FR-064.title: Active-controller status MUST NOT grant access to any private game-master operation.

FR-065.title: Accepted active-controller actions MUST continue to follow all existing password, likeness, attempt, special-pattern, dud-removal, restoration, lockout, navigation, and content rules.

FR-066.title: Character claims, player actions, controller changes, roster changes, and active-terminal changes MUST have one unambiguous authoritative order.

FR-067.title: An action ordered before controller reassignment MUST be evaluated using the former controller's authority at that processing point.

FR-068.title: An action ordered after controller reassignment MUST be rejected when submitted by the former controller.

FR-069.title: A race between action processing and reassignment MUST NOT produce duplicate or unauthorized canonical mutation.

FR-070.title: After submitting a shared action, player input MUST enter a pending state until an authoritative outcome is applied.

FR-071.title: Player clients MUST NOT optimistically mutate canonical shared state.

FR-072.title: The authoritative outcome of an accepted or rejected action MUST end its pending state without relying only on an arbitrary animation delay.

FR-073.title: Rapid duplicate submissions for a one-use action MUST produce no more than one accepted mutation.

FR-074.title: Every connected assigned session MUST receive accepted terminal navigation, hacking state, logs, loading transitions, and outcomes from the same canonical state.

FR-075.title: All tabs belonging to one logical session MUST receive the same assignment and controller status changes.

FR-076.title: The game master MUST determine which single configured terminal, if any, is currently presented to players.

FR-077.title: Activating another terminal MUST transition every connected player automatically through the existing terminal loading presentation.

FR-078.title: Active-terminal switching MUST preserve logical sessions, character assignments, and controller assignment.

FR-079.title: A newly assigned player MUST join the terminal currently selected by the game master.

FR-080.title: When no terminal is active during a broadcast, assigned sessions MUST retain identity and assignment while seeing an immersive waiting state.

FR-081.title: An inactive terminal MUST reject player actions until it becomes active again.

FR-082.title: Requesting a switch away from an unfinished puzzle MUST pause the switch for an explicit preserve, discard, or cancel decision by the game master.

FR-083.title: Choosing preserve MUST suspend the unfinished puzzle in process-local state and make it unable to receive player actions while inactive.

FR-084.title: Reactivating a terminal with a preserved puzzle MUST restore its exact board, remaining attempts, removed duds, available and used patterns, progress log, and outcome.

FR-085.title: Choosing discard MUST cause the terminal's next hacking attempt to create a fresh puzzle under the existing generation rules.

FR-086.title: Choosing cancel MUST leave the current terminal and unfinished puzzle active and unchanged.

FR-087.title: The system MUST NOT silently discard, solve, fail, restart, or otherwise alter an unfinished puzzle during a terminal-switch request.

FR-088.title: The private game-master application MUST show every currently connected logical session with its fallback name, character assignment if any, presence, and controller-or-observer status.

FR-089.title: The private game-master application MUST keep a disconnected active session visibly identified until it reconnects or control is reassigned.

FR-090.title: The game-master session view MUST show both fallback session name and character name when needed to resolve device or assignment problems.

FR-091.title: Character name MUST remain the primary player-facing identity after assignment, while fallback session name remains a separate technical label.

FR-092.title: Ending a broadcast MUST remove the active terminal from player control and return connected clients to an immersive waiting or selection state.

FR-093.title: Ending a broadcast MUST NOT delete configured terminals or silently alter durable unlocked-terminal state.

FR-094.title: Server restart MUST discard logical sessions, fallback-name changes, presence, character claims, controller assignment, and any active runtime puzzle allowed to expire by the existing persistence boundary.

FR-095.title: The game-master application MUST retain its existing trusted operations regardless of player connection, assignment, or controller state.

FR-096.title: This feature MUST NOT redesign existing terminal or hacking logs to add historical character ownership.

FR-097.title: This feature MUST NOT add accounts, authentication, persistent player profiles, individual invitation links, unassigned spectators, multiple simultaneous controllers, or automatic controller election after disconnect.

FR-098.title: This feature MUST NOT import or manage character sheets, attributes, skills, perks, eligibility, rules tests, inventory, or campaign history.

FR-099.title: This feature MUST NOT change existing password-guessing, likeness, attempt, special-pattern, dud-removal, attempt-restoration, lockout, terminal-content, or game-master success rules.

context: area: existing live broadcast, player server, protocol, and master/player presentation
constraint: behavior-focused only; storage, protocol fields, synchronization primitive, package, and schema design deferred to plan
constraint: preserve all existing hacking, terminal-content, and ForceHackSuccess rules
intent: Coordinate one character per logical player session and one authorized terminal controller while every other assigned player observes the same canonical live broadcast.
expectations: No user accounts, passwords, or authentication
No character sheets, campaign profiles, or Fallout 2d20 rules automation
No hacking-eligibility validation
No individual invitation links
No new internet exposure or access control beyond the existing setup
No unassigned spectator access
No simultaneous control by multiple logical sessions
No automatic controller election after disconnect
No logical-session persistence across server restarts
No character-claim persistence across broadcasts
No persistent connection or character action history
No per-terminal controller assignments
No hacking-difficulty changes
No special-pattern rule changes
No ordinary password-guess or filler-click rule changes
No ForceHackSuccess behavior changes
No terminal-content rule changes
No new Fallout or CRT visual redesign
No new localization or audio systems
No mobile-phone-specific presentation
approach: Introduce one process-local control coordinator that serializes logical-session presence, roster and claims, controller authority, terminal switching, and player actions while delegating unchanged terminal mechanics to internal/live. Publish detached revisioned master/player projections and correlated action results, keep recognition in a server-issued same-origin browser token, and preserve the version-1 persistence and private ForceHackSuccess boundaries.

decisions.decision: Use one outer internal/control coordinator for every game-master and player transition
decisions.why: Claims, controller changes, actions, and switches require one mutation and publication order across concurrent Wails and WebSocket callers
decisions.rejected: Separately locked roster, authorization, and live-state services

decisions.decision: Use a server-issued browser token in same-origin localStorage, separate from the process-local logical session ID
decisions.why: It supports refresh, reopen, and multi-tab continuity while stale tokens after restart restore no state
decisions.rejected: Raw connection IDs, persisted accounts, or sessionStorage

decisions.decision: Separate process, broadcast, and active-terminal lifetimes
decisions.why: Sessions and roster survive broadcast end, claims and controller do not, and a broadcast may have no active terminal
decisions.rejected: Per-terminal assignments or treating terminal clear as broadcast end

decisions.decision: Checkpoint the complete private terminal runtime for preserve and refresh authored content on reactivation
decisions.why: Exact puzzle restoration requires secret and generation-bound state that public projections omit
decisions.rejected: Reconstructing from public state or silently discarding on switch/delete

decisions.decision: Require requestId, broadcastId, and terminalId preconditions and return revisioned ACTION_RESULT outcomes
decisions.why: Stale and duplicate requests must not mutate a later broadcast or terminal, and pending input must end authoritatively on acceptance or rejection
decisions.rejected: Animation timeouts or uncorrelated later snapshots

decisions.decision: Use complete personalized PLAYER_STATE and one complete coordination-state master snapshot
decisions.why: Role and roster state are personalized while complete revisioned snapshots avoid reconnect gaps and mixed-revision UI
decisions.rejected: Broadcasting private master session data or many partially ordered deltas

decisions.why: The standard library and existing deterministic Go and Playwright infrastructure cover identifiers, ordering, protocol, and browser behavior
decisions.rejected: A database, frontend framework, or second browser-test tool

plan.summary: Planned one ordered process-local coordination layer with strict revisioned Wails and WebSocket contracts
plan.key_finding: Current live mutations are mutex-protected, but their Wails and WebSocket publications occur across separate caller paths and can overtake each other; authorization and publication must share one outer transaction.

tasks.summary: 115 tasks across Setup, Foundational, nine user-story phases, and Polish; every phase uses explicit test-first dependency waves and all FR-001 through FR-099 are mapped.

T001.did: Broadened Playwright discovery to all browser specs without changing its worker or server configuration.

T004.did: Specified strict handshake, selection, request-precondition, personalized-state, action-result, and revisioned terminal protocol contracts.

T003.did: Added coordinator foundation contract tests for deterministic IDs, revision rules, detached effects, and enqueue ordering

T002.did: Added failing-first deep-detachment and version-1 runtime-persistence boundary tests for coordination projections

T008.did: Added concurrency-safe deterministic opaque-ID and ordered-effect fakes with call/order inspection and context-aware waiting
